hints: Focus on what functional groups release a combustible gas with sodium, and what structural feature is needed for the iodoform test.
Recall that both $\text{-OH}$ in alcohols and $\text{-COOH}$ in carboxylic acids give $\text{H}_2$ with $\text{Na}$, so check each of 1, 2 and 3 for this first.
Now test each compound for $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ groups, since only those give yellow $\text{CHI}_3$, and see which ones correctly give no precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Understand the sodium test**

Think of sodium as a detector for acidic protons. Both alcohols and carboxylic acids react to release hydrogen, which burns.

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCOOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Understand the iodoform test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate only with a methyl-adjacent oxidisable group. That is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ in alcohols or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ in carbonyl compounds. Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is the only primary alcohol that is positive.

**Check compound 1, ethanoic acid**

$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ has an acidic proton, so it gives $\text{H}_2$ with $\text{Na}$. It does not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ and carboxylic acids do not give iodoform, so no yellow precipitate. Statement 1 fits.

**Check compound 2, pentan-3-ol**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a secondary alcohol, so it gives $\text{H}_2$ with $\text{Na}$. The $\text{-OH}$ carbon is attached to two $\text{CH}_2$ groups, not a $\text{CH}_3$ group, so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$. Statement 2 fits.

**Check compound 3, propan-1-ol**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is a primary alcohol, so it gives $\text{H}_2$ with $\text{Na}$. It is not ethanol and has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group, so it gives no yellow precipitate. Statement 3 fits.

**Conclude**

All three compounds satisfy both conditions: reaction with sodium plus negative iodoform test. So 1, 2 and 3 are all possible identities for Z.

options.A: Correct, because 1, 2 and 3 are all valid. Each has $\text{O-H}$ to give $\text{H}_2$ with sodium, and none has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ structure needed for a positive iodoform test.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 and 2 are correct, leaving out propan-1-ol. Students choose this if they wrongly think all primary alcohols except methanol give iodoform, but only ethanol does.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean only 2 and 3 are correct, leaving out ethanoic acid. Students choose this if they forget carboxylic acids also react with sodium to give $\text{H}_2$, or think ethanoic acid gives iodoform because it contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 is correct. Students choose this if they confuse pentan-3-ol with pentan-2-ol, which does contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ and would give a positive iodoform test, and so wrongly reject 2 and 3.
